categories.title: Spreadsheets and documents
categories.goodFor: Total flexibility, familiar to everyone, and free or close to it.
categories.gap: Numbers only stay current if someone updates them, and nothing tells you what changed or what needs a decision.
categories.trenston: Trenston reads from the tools you connect, shows a Briefing of what changed, and puts open decisions in a ranked queue.

categories.title: Dashboards and reporting tools
categories.goodFor: Pulling data from many sources into clear charts.
categories.gap: They usually stop at showing what happened. Deciding what to do, and handing it to someone, tends to happen somewhere else.
categories.trenston: Trenston adds a Decision Center that ranks open calls with a recommendation and confidence score, and lets you delegate the follow-up to an owner.

categories.title: Enterprise suites and ERP systems
categories.goodFor: Depth, process control and scale for large organizations.
categories.gap: They can take significant time and budget to set up, and are often built around dedicated administrators.
categories.trenston: Trenston is built for the founder or CEO. Start free, explore a built-in demo company before you set anything up, and connect your accounting system, including SAP Business One, instead of replacing it.

categories.title: Chat and project tools
categories.gap: Company-wide numbers and open decisions end up spread across threads and boards.
categories.trenston: Trenston keeps tasks, decisions, financial figures and department work in one workspace, and can post high-severity alerts to a Slack channel.

rows.common: Open several tools and piece it together.
rows.trenston: One workspace with a Briefing, financials, pipeline, tasks and department queues.

rows.common: Work it out yourself from the numbers.
rows.trenston: The Decision Center ranks open decisions, drafts a recommendation with a confidence score, and waits for you to confirm.

rows.common: Message the person and hope it gets tracked.
rows.trenston: Assign it to an owner in Tasks or a department. Assignees get an email when work is delegated to them.

rows.common: Empty cells can be mistaken for zeros.
rows.trenston: Shows "Add data" instead of a made-up zero.

rows.common: Build a formula, filter or report.
rows.trenston: Ask Trenston in plain English. It answers from the data in your workspace and is instructed to say when something has not been entered.

rows.common: A separate tool for each team.
rows.trenston: Sales, Production, Procurement, Maintenance, Legal, HR and Finance, linked together. For example, a procurement request can show that it is blocking a production order.

rows.common: Often set up by hand, file by file.
rows.trenston: Role-based access. People see their own departments, and financial data is limited to people granted Financials access.

notList: Not accounting software. Trenston reads from QuickBooks, Xero or SAP Business One. It does not replace your books.
Not a full ERP. It tracks work across departments, but it does not run payroll, inventory valuation or manufacturing planning.
Not a full CRM. It can pull deals from HubSpot into Pipeline and Telemetry.
Not legal advice. The Legal department tracks matters and deadlines. It does not advise.
Not on autopilot. Suggestions are drafts, and nothing becomes a decision until you confirm it.
Early. Trenston is a young product, and we only list what is live today. The Integrations page spells out exactly what each connection does.
betterElsewhere: You need payroll, tax filing or full double-entry accounting. Use dedicated accounting software, and connect it to Trenston.
You need heavy custom reporting for a data team. A dedicated analytics tool will go further.
You run a large organization with complex process control. An enterprise suite is built for that.
You want one flexible blank canvas. A spreadsheet is hard to beat.
disclaimer: This page describes general types of tools, not any specific product. Individual products differ and change over time. Statements about Trenston reflect the product as of October 2026.
